Paper.title: A Graph Neural Network for Global Daily Fire Radiative Power Prediction at Medium-Range Lead Times
Paper.authors: Li Zhang, Jun Wang, Isidora Jankov et al. (NOAA / CU Boulder)

Paper.title: Learning joint probabilistic weather forecasts from station observations alone (CLARA)
Paper.authors: Chaeyeon Yi, Yun Am Seo (HUFS / Jeju National University)

Paper.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Atmospheric Rivers in GraphCast
Paper.authors: Madelyn Mathai et al. (University of Virginia)

Claim.text: 7-day-ahead global fire forecast error is significantly below the operational persistence forecast
Operational fire-source data is severely stale
A tiny model can produce joint probabilistic forecasts
Inter-variable correlation is real information, not decoration
Nobody taught it IVT, yet GraphCast internally computes it stably
The strongest concept tracks atmospheric river intensity
The concepts are actually used by the model, not bystander correlations

Evidence.text: 0.1deg MSE: 2023 lead-1 -32%, lead-7 -43%; 2024 -24% and -40% vs persistence
Satellite fire product has ~1.5 day latency and is then frozen unchanged through the following 5 days of operational forecasts (7 days frozen in the experimental version)
1deg fire-detection critical success index 0.32-0.60, decaying only slowly with lead time
Training and testing both use the GBBEPx product definition
~28k parameters; trains 40 epochs in 2.1 min on a regular CPU; one 96-station forecast takes 0.43 ms

Retrained in 10 regions on six continents: wins all 60 region-lead comparisons vs persistence, 57 vs same-scale learning models; energy score 4.9% below same-input rivals, 11%-65% below statistical baselines
Ablation: removing learned correlations (variance only) worsens joint-forecast negative log-likelihood by 1.0-2.8 per station
Consistency proof exists for the covariance scale estimator
IVT never appears as input or forecast target, yet is stably detected in internal activations; concepts persist across processor depths

Concept 99 'global atmospheric river' correlates 0.51 (time-mean) with regional maximum IVT; concept 1592 responds specifically to strong North-American west-coast IVT; concepts form a parent-child hierarchy (99 is a parent)
Directly intervening on internal activations changes the forecast accordingly
Code is open source and reproducible

Counterexample.text: The advantage grows with lead time because the 'no-change' assumption degrades faster - it does not mean high absolute 7-day accuracy

Scope limit (not a counter-result): the staleness described covers one operational chain only - NOAA GEFS-Aerosols initialised from GBBEPx; fire inputs at other centres are outside this claim's coverage

Large-fire radiative power is systematically underestimated; small-fire locations are often wrong - intensity calibration and small-fire localisation are the authors' own two 'lessons before deployment'
Real operational observation noise and product version changes not covered; preprint, not peer-reviewed
Scope limit (not a counter-result): validated only at the scale of 96 stations, 1-48 h leads and five variables; no evidence in this paper at operational grid scale
Wins are against persistence and same-scale baselines; never faced an operational-grade NWP system head-on
Authors' own caveat: attention bias coefficients cannot be read directly as causal evidence of which station influenced a forecast
At long leads the proof's premises break first, causing over-correction; joint distribution assumes Gaussianity, extreme tails (where compound disasters live) may be poorly described; preprint
Correlation 0.51 evidences that the concept is detected, not the model's computational precision for IVT

Scope limit (not a counter-result): the time-mean correlation is 0.51, so a single strongest concept still leaves most IVT variance unexplained; responses are regional (concept 1592 is specific to strong North-American west-coast IVT)
Intervention evidence is complete only for the atmospheric-river phenomenon class
Fully validated only on atmospheric rivers; fronts, blocking highs and other phenomena unverified; preprint

Method.text: Spatiotemporal GNN (grid cells linked by geographic proximity); inputs: historical fire points + reanalysis meteorology + land cover/vegetation; trained 2020-2022, fully held-out test 2023 and 2024; baseline: operational persistence forecast.
Wind-direction-biased attention (upwind positions back-tracked by lead time, weights decay with lead) + five-variable joint Gaussian output; station observations only, no NWP or reanalysis inputs.

Sparse autoencoders (Matryoshka variant) fitted at GraphCast processor layers 0/8/15 as a 'concept dictionary' (512-dim activations -> 4096 entries); concepts matched against real atmospheric phenomena, with internal activation interventions to test causality.

Dataset.text: GBBEPx satellite fire radiative power (FRP) product
Korean automatic weather station system, 96 stations; lead times 1-48h in six bands
GraphCast internal activations vs atmospheric river phenomena and IVT (integrated vapour transport) diagnostics
